Cascade Mutual — Medical Policy: MRI Lumbar Spine (CPT 72148)
## Definitions
- **conservative management**: a documented trial of non-surgical care including physical therapy, NSAIDs, and activity modification
- **red-flag features**: clinical findings suggesting malignancy, spinal infection, fracture, or cauda equina syndrome
- **radiculopathy**: radiating pain, numbness, or weakness following a nerve-root distribution

Cascade Mutual — Medical Policy: MRI Lumbar Spine (CPT 72148)
## Coverage Criteria
Cascade Mutual considers mri lumbar spine medically necessary when the referral documents any of the following:
- Low back pain or lumbar radiculopathy persisting at least 6 weeks despite documented conservative management
- Progressive neurologic deficit or objective motor weakness on examination
- Clinical suspicion of malignancy, spinal infection, or cauda equina syndrome
- Preoperative planning in a documented surgical candidate

Cascade Mutual — Medical Policy: MRI Lumbar Spine (CPT 72148)
## Exceptions and Expedited Review
When progressive neurologic deficit, suspected cauda equina syndrome, or clinical suspicion of malignancy or infection is documented, the conservative-management waiting period is waived and the request is routed to expedited review.

Cascade Mutual — Medical Policy: MRI Lumbar Spine (CPT 72148)
## Background
MRI of the lumbar spine evaluates the intervertebral discs, spinal canal, and nerve roots. Because most acute low back pain resolves with first-line care, advanced imaging is reserved for patients whose symptoms persist despite an adequate treatment trial or who present with findings suggesting serious underlying pathology.

Northgate Plan — Medical Policy: CT Chest (CPT 71260)
## Coverage Criteria
Northgate Plan considers ct chest medically necessary when the referral documents any of the following:
- Structured follow-up of a pulmonary nodule identified on prior imaging
- Chronic cough or hemoptysis with clinical suspicion of malignancy
- Evaluation of a known or suspected thoracic mass, lymphadenopathy, or interstitial disease
- Staging of a known malignancy

Northgate Plan — Medical Policy: CT Chest (CPT 71260)
## Definitions
- **pulmonary nodule**: a discrete rounded opacity up to 3 cm identified on prior imaging
- **structured follow-up**: interval imaging performed on a recognized nodule-surveillance schedule

Northgate Plan — Medical Policy: CT Chest (CPT 71260)
## Background
CT of the chest with contrast evaluates the lung parenchyma, mediastinum, and thoracic vasculature. It is used to characterize findings seen on prior imaging or to investigate symptoms suspicious for malignancy or thoracic disease.

Northgate Plan — Medical Policy: CT Chest (CPT 71260)
## Non-Covered and Exclusions
Northgate Plan does not consider the study medically necessary in the following circumstances:
- Routine screening outside an approved lung-cancer screening program
- Acute uncomplicated upper-respiratory infection

- Imaging in asymptomatic patients for screening purposes
